author: simulation_agent

system_configuration.model: overdamped Brownian dynamics of N identical particles in two dimensions in a periodic box, purely repulsive Yukawa pair potential u(r) = U0 (a/r) exp(-kappa (r - a)) with U0 = Gamma k_B T and kappa = kappa_a / a, no hydrodynamic interactions, no attraction, no wall, no drive; positions start uniformly random; temperature enters as the noise amplitude only

actions.action: per cell and seed: place n_particles uniformly at random in the periodic box Lx = rows_x * lattice_constant, Ly = rows_y * sqrt(3)/2 * lattice_constant, with U0 = gamma * k_B * temperature and kappa = kappa_a / mean_spacing, cutoff where u/kT falls below one thousandth
integrate overdamped Brownian dynamics at integration_timestep, saving wrapped positions every save_interval, until the psi6 stop criterion fires or run_time_cap is reached

per frame compute psi6 per particle from its Voronoi neighbours using wrapped positions under the minimum image, average over particles; fit the plateau over the last relaxation_fit_window of the record; report the first time psi6(t) reaches plateau_fraction of it, per seed, and the mean and block standard error over seeds per cell

envelope_check.note: target local: every cost number of this plan that lines up with a ceiling is under it: wall_clock_estimate against wall_clock_max, storage_estimate against storage_max. Re-confirmed at run time (4.6 O1).

cost.wall_clock: of order two hours for the whole sweep at the assumed rate of ten million particle-steps a second; the rate has never been measured for this model and the smoke run does that first
cost.note: the estimate is arithmetic over the chosen point; the rate under it is A5's assumption. The frame-writing cost is not in the model and at a hundred frames a run is small here

stop_criteria.statement: the relaxation is complete when the particle-averaged psi6 first reaches the declared fraction of its plateau; the time at which it does is the observable
the run ends at the cap without the plateau criterion having fired; it is kept and reported NOT CONVERGED, and its relaxation time is a lower bound, not a value
a particle moving more than a lattice constant in one step is a diverged integration; stop and keep the run, because divergence is a result

success_criteria.statement: in every seed of a cell the plateau criterion fired before the cap; a cell where it did not is reported as not converged and enters no comparison as a value

success_criteria.window: over the seeds of one cell
success_criteria.statement: the seed-to-seed spread of the relaxation time, as a standard error of the cell mean, is inside the ten per cent the design asked for

alternatives_rejected.what: a timestep per sweep cell (the bounds carry varies_with)
alternatives_rejected.reason: one step at the stiffest cell's bound keeps every cell under the same integrator settings, so a difference between cells cannot be an integrator difference; the cost of that choice is a factor of a few at the weak cells and the total still sits under the ceiling

alternatives_rejected.what: the noise-step and Brownian-time bounds on the timestep
alternatives_rejected.reason: both are looser than the curvature bound at every cell of this sweep, so the curvature bound is the one that binds

alternatives_rejected.what: more seeds than the statistics floor
alternatives_rejected.reason: ten per cent statistical error is met at nine seeds and the budget margin does not allow a decade more
bd_pairwise_driven_tracer imposes a drive and this goal carries no `drive` selector; bd_pairwise is the configuration for an undriven question

open_risks: The run cap is ten Brownian times and ordering from a random start in a stiff Yukawa system may take a hundred; a cell that ends on the cap is a lower bound and the first thing the result reports.
The particle-step rate under the cost estimate is a guess about this workstation; the smoke run measures it, and the full sweep is not submitted until that measurement is in a card.

Finite size is never absent here: the psi6 correlation length grows toward the box as the structure orders. The design margin is thirty spacings and its falsifier is a second box a factor of two larger giving the same time, which is a separate plan.
The plateau fraction 0.9 is the design stage's convention until a person chooses one; the vocabulary's window field holds only the fit window, so this card carries the fraction as a condition.
Nothing here is fitted to experimental data and no experimental counterpart exists for this observable; the anchor on the lab's particles is what would make one comparable.
Temperature is a coordinate of the model and not a measurement of it: the integrator represents no velocity, so the declared value enters as the noise amplitude and cannot fail to be realised.

numbers.name: run_time_cap
numbers.note: ten Brownian times

numbers.name: relaxation_fit_window
numbers.note: the observable's declared window: the plateau is read over this many seconds of frames

numbers.name: plateau_fraction
numbers.note: the fraction of the psi6 plateau at which the relaxation time is read; a condition the plan carries, because the vocabulary's window_parameter holds only the fit window

numbers.name: lattice_constant
numbers.note: the triangular lattice constant at the reference density, a_lat**2 * sqrt(3)/2 = a**2

numbers.name: rows_x
numbers.note: lattice columns along x; the box is rows_x * lattice_constant wide, derived by the backend

numbers.name: rows_y
numbers.note: lattice rows along y, even, so the triangular lattice closes periodically; the box is rows_y * sqrt(3)/2 * lattice_constant tall

numbers.name: n_seeds_point
numbers.note: at the statistics floor, because the budget below is tight

numbers.name: gamma_min
numbers.note: the weakest coupling of the sweep

numbers.name: gamma_max
numbers.note: the largest coupling U0/kT of the sweep; the stiff corner the timestep must survive

numbers.name: kappa_a_min
numbers.note: the longest range of the sweep

numbers.name: kappa_a_max
numbers.note: the shortest range of the sweep, as kappa times the mean spacing

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: the room's reading, not the sample's. In the model it is a parameter of the noise amplitude and exact; the reason to use the room's value is to match the lab

numbers.name: viscosity
numbers.note: pure water near 293 K, textbook; the entry's own precision is of-order

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the lab's particles, measured by the operator on 2026-09-19 (CV at most 2 per cent). Taken from the store under the S2 id as the physical-units anchor; see the constraint note on anchoring

numbers.name: diffusivity
numbers.note: the free diffusivity D0 of one particle in the bath; the Brownian time at the mean spacing, a^2/D0, is the natural time unit of the relaxation and every axis derives it from this

numbers.name: mean_spacing
numbers.note: a = rho**-1/2 at the reference density; the density sweep moves it by less than a decade

numbers.name: brownian_time
numbers.note: the time to diffuse one spacing: the natural unit of structural relaxation here, and NOT tau_d, which is the time to diffuse one diameter and belongs to the free-tracer question

numbers.name: dt_max_noise
numbers.note: sqrt(2 D0 dt) must stay inside the potential's range or a step carries a particle across it in one move

numbers.name: dt_max_brownian
numbers.note: the bound the free-tracer configuration would have stopped at; here it is the loosest of three

numbers.name: n_seeds_min
numbers.note: independent samples are SEEDS: one run gives one relaxation time, because psi6(t) is already averaged over every particle

numbers.name: n_particles_min
numbers.note: (L/a)**2 at the reference density

numbers.name: particle_steps_total
numbers.note: against particle_steps_max 7e10: inside, by a margin that is not a decade. The cost per particle-step behind the ceiling is a guess; the smoke run measures it

numbers.name: particle_steps_max
numbers.note: the product n_particles * steps * n_seeds * sweep_points must sit under this

numbers.name: particle_frames_total
numbers.note: against particle_frames_max 5e8: two decades inside

numbers.name: particle_step_rate
numbers.note: particle-steps per wall second for a 2D neighbour-list Brownian integrator on this workstation's CPU. The store's agreed name and unit (a rate, not a time per step), so a measured timing entry lands here when one exists

numbers.name: drive_selectors_on_goal
numbers.note: the goal carries no `drive` selector; the count is zero and is written as arithmetic on a carried number so the validator can recompute it. It is the ground on which the driven configuration is rejected for this question

numbers.name: steps_per_run
numbers.note: one timestep for every cell, set at the stiffest cell's bound; a per-cell step would be cheaper and is recorded as rejected below

numbers.name: gamma_levels
numbers.note: two levels: the sweep's two corners, 10 and 100

numbers.name: kappa_a_levels
numbers.note: two levels: 1 and 3, the range's two ends; the range spans half a decade so one level per decade gives its endpoints

numbers.name: fit_window_frames_min
numbers.note: saved frames the relaxation_fit_window must span

numbers.name: storage_per_particle_frame
numbers.note: two double coordinates per particle per frame

numbers.name: target_rel_error
numbers.note: statistical error on the relaxation time at one sweep point; inside a decade with room to spare

numbers.name: wall_clock_estimate
numbers.note: the whole sweep, four cells times nine seeds, at the assumed rate; the smoke run measures the rate

assumptions.statement: The sweep corners. Revision 1 left them to the design stage, which took Gamma up to 1000 and kappa a up to 10 and refused on budget: one sweep point at that corner needed of order 8e11 particle-steps against 7e10. The relaxation option it attached -- Gamma 10 to 100, kappa a 1 to 3 -- was put to the person, who ruled for it on 2026-09-23. So these four numbers are the person's decision carried as an assumption, not the design stage's own; the store still holds nothing about a 2D Yukawa sweep range, which is the gap named here.
assumptions.falsifier: a first run showing psi6 already at its plateau at the lowest coupling, or unreachable inside the cap at the highest, moves the corresponding end by a decade -- with the person's word, since the corners are now theirs

assumptions.statement: Nine tenths of the plateau is high enough that the structure is recognisably ordered and low enough that the approach is not dominated by the last defects annealing, whose time is a different quantity. A threshold nobody has chosen is UNDECIDED and not satisfied; this is S3's choice, written down so S4 and the plan carry it as a condition.
assumptions.falsifier: a person choosing the fraction, or the vocabulary gaining a second window parameter for it

assumptions.statement: A window of fewer than ten frames fits a plateau through noise.
assumptions.falsifier: a fit over a shorter window giving the same time within error

assumptions.statement: Of order ten million particle-steps per second is what a CPU neighbour-list integrator with a short-ranged pair force manages; nothing on this machine has measured it for this potential. The frame-writing cost is not in this model yet (task 023 is adding a per-particle-frame term); at a hundred frames a run it is small here, and the smoke run measures both.
assumptions.falsifier: a smoke run of this configuration that writes its trajectory replaces this with its own log's wall time per particle-step

assumptions.statement: Positions only, in double precision, two coordinates in 2D.
assumptions.falsifier: the trajectory writer's declared frame format replaces the estimate

assumptions.statement: Ten per cent is a tenth of the decade explore mode answers in, so the statistical error never decides a comparison between sweep points.
assumptions.falsifier: a person stating a target accuracy replaces it

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.

The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.
